content: AI decision-making encompasses methods that enable machines to make choices or predictions based on data and programmed objectives. Several approaches guide AI decision processes, including rule-based systems that follow explicit if-then logic; statistical methods that use probability to handle uncertainty; utility-based approaches that maximize expected outcomes; and learning-based systems that improve through experience. Planning algorithms help AI navigate complex decision spaces by considering possible future states and action sequences. These include search algorithms like A* that find optimal paths by evaluating states based on current cost and estimated distance to goals, and Monte Carlo Tree Search that samples possible action sequences to identify promising strategies. Decision trees represent choices and consequences in a hierarchical structure, with each branch representing a possible decision and resulting outcome. Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) model sequential decision problems where outcomes depend partly on chance, using reward functions to represent desirability of different states. Reinforcement learning agents make decisions to maximize cumulative rewards through trial and error, developing policies that map situations to actions. Bayesian networks represent probabilistic relationships between variables, enabling inference under uncertainty by calculating conditional probabilities. Multi-agent systems consider interactions between multiple decision-makers, requiring game theory to model strategic thinking. Modern AI often combines multiple approaches: reinforcement learning with neural networks enables complex pattern recognition for decision-making; ensemble methods integrate predictions from multiple algorithms for improved accuracy; and hierarchical systems decompose complex decisions into manageable sub-decisions, reflective of human cognitive processes.

scenario.title: Adventure Decision Navigator
scenario.content: Students experience an interactive narrative where AI agents make decisions that shape story outcomes. The simulation allows students to implement different decision-making approachesâfrom simple rule-based systems to sophisticated reinforcement learning agentsâand observe how these methods handle narrative branches and consequences. The system visualizes decision processes, showing search trees, utility calculations, probability distributions, or neural network activations depending on the approach used. Students can create decision scenarios, define reward structures, and train agents to navigate complex choice environments. Interactive tools demonstrate how agents evaluate options, plan sequences, handle uncertainty, and learn from experience. Challenge modes task students with designing agents that achieve specific narrative outcomes or adapt to changing environmental conditions, teaching fundamental principles of computational decision-making while engaging students through storytelling.

hypothesis.description: Students will implement AI decision algorithms by designing agents that navigate complex choice environments. They will analyze how different approaches handle uncertainty and sequential planning, and develop appropriate decision methods for varying problem structures and information conditions.
